title: Hot Cocoa Mix

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no events or price change (price unchanged at $5.03). The baseline median is 22.6. Recent weeks show no trend or seasonal ramp; the last promotion was 3 weeks ago (2026-05-25), and the classical uplift model suggests a 25% drop in the following week (x0.75), but this effect is already partially reflected in the baseline (recent sales: 22, 17, 24). The noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is only x1.08, and the 'after' effect is x0.75, but the evidence is thin (only 5 past occurrences). The product's ordinary noise is ±37%, so a single past dip is not a driver. No named drivers justify an adjustment. The classical uplift model’s x0.75 is too strong and not supported by the noise-adjusted evidence. The week is ordinary.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-37% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
